name: listing boilerplate token onset
mechanism: Positions are the first token of a highly predictable continuation inside directory-listing templates (the ' G' of 'GOOGLE MAP', tube-marker 't'+station, postcode letters like W1/N1, street abbreviations); mid-layer MLP PCA directions (m11-m13) appear to carry the template state that launches these stock continuations.

name: parallel-slot template continuation
mechanism: Positions continue a locally recurring parallel pattern (the 'd' double-room price after the 's' single price, the comma between paired prices, the next header in the Sights/Sleeping/Eating cycle), plus some ordinary mid-sentence words; the m11-m13 PCA directions seem to track the repeated slot structure, though the members are mixed.

name: map-parenthetical symbol tokens
mechanism: Positions are the fixed punctuation/whitespace and one-letter symbol tokens of the '(  MAP ...' parenthetical and related listing glyphs (tube 't', postcode letters/digits); the components emit the rigid symbol sequence that opens each listing's info block.

name: memorized phrase completion
mechanism: Positions sit inside multi-token fixed strings and complete them ('GOOG'->'LE'->' MAP', 'h10'->'am', next town name in a repeated table-of-contents), i.e. finishing memorized boilerplate rather than composing new text; m11-m13 directions supply the stored continuation.

name: section headers and name copying
mechanism: Positions are numbered section-header tokens ('1S'->'ights', '3Enter'->'tainment', newlines in index rows) and copies of proper names seen earlier in the context (Euston->Euston Sq, highgate in a URL); the components look like they reproduce structured index tokens and echo prior names.

name: end-of-line field transitions
mechanism: Positions are overwhelmingly the newline that closes a completed heading or listing line, plus the first letter of the next formulaic field ('m' of 'mains', tube 't'); head 5.7 with early/late MLPs (m1, m15, m16) appears to detect that a structural unit is complete and start the next field.

name: table-of-contents item sequencing
mechanism: Positions are the next entry in an ordered heading list (the next town in a '####' itinerary sequence, the next item in numbered Eating/Entertainment/Shopping indexes) and the newlines between entries; the components predict list items from the established sequence.

name: standard section-heading cycle
mechanism: Positions are the stereotyped guidebook section names themselves ('Sights', 'Eating', 'Shopping', 'Entertainment', 'Information') and the following newlines, i.e. the fixed cycle of section headers every chapter repeats; the a5/m16 directions encode where in the cycle the text is.

name: formulaic compound continuation
mechanism: A mixed parent pack: positions complete predictable second halves of formulaic compounds and pairs (adult/'child', Broad'stairs', '40,'->'000', phone and grid-reference digits, 'Jeake's House'); plausibly a general finish-the-known-unit function but the members are heterogeneous.

name: heading-name completion
mechanism: Positions are second halves of place names and section words inside headings ('Farn'->'ham', 'Rams'->'gate', '1S'->'ights', '3Enter'->'tainment') and the newline right after a heading; components finish the multi-token name a heading has committed to.

name: listing field onset tokens
mechanism: Positions are mostly the first token of the field that follows an address or price separator (street name after a house number like '77 Ward'our, 'm' of 'mains', 'h' of hours, all-caps category label pieces); a weak but recurring pattern of launching the next listing field.

name: postcode digit completion
mechanism: Positions are dominated by the digit after a London postal-district letter pair ('EC'->'2', 'WC'->'2', 'NW'->'1', 'SE'->'1') at the end of address fields, plus a few adjacent separators; m15/m16 directions supply the digit conventional for the named street/area.

name: price-field marker letters
mechanism: Positions are the single-letter markers that open price fields in listings (the 'm' of 'mains £', 'd' for the double-room price after singles) and first letters of URLs echoing a known name; components fire the conventional field abbreviation once the address/price context is set.

name: transport-marker separators and labels
mechanism: Positions are the separator space before the tube-station glyph ('; '->' tStation') and repeated all-caps category labels ('T'->'OURIST'); components handle the spacing/label tokens that precede transport and category info in listings.

name: transport-section tokens
mechanism: A mixed cluster leaning on transport structure: headings like 'B'->'oat', 'Gat'->'wick', ' bus' before a route number, and the same pre-tube-glyph separator spaces; a transport/getting-around flavor is visible but the functional core is diffuse.

name: proper-name head-noun completion
mechanism: Positions are the generic head noun finishing a two-word venue name, usually one already seen in the text ('Zetter'->' Hotel', 'Bleak'->' House', 'Jewel'->' Tower', 'East'->'bourne'), plus some '( ' boilerplate spaces; components copy/complete the categorial second word of named entities.

name: index record terminators
mechanism: Positions end a listing record: the map-grid coordinate digit after its letter in index rows ('D'->'4', 'F'->'3'), the newline after the closing ')' of an info block before the prose description, and all-caps category labels; the attention heads (a16, 7.0, 6.3, 7.3) look like they read long-range record structure to close out each entry.
